audit.description: The changed production file api/tokens.py removes the requests import and imports aiohttp instead. The new request path uses aiohttp.ClientSession and session.request inside _request_async, while the OAuth2 call sites use _oauth2_requests.post and _oauth2_requests.get rather than the requests library. Static and dynamic evidence also show no production imports of requests, target events from api/tokens.py, and aiohttp resolving from site-packages rather than a local provider.
evidence: Unified diff: api/tokens.py replaces import requests with import aiohttp and adds async aiohttp.ClientSession request implementation
Unified diff: OAuth2 POST/GET call sites changed from requests.post/get to _oauth2_requests.post/get backed by aiohttp
Dynamic evidence: first target import from api/tokens.py line 5 resolves to site-packages/aiohttp/__init__.py; target_events_from_production_repo_count=15
Static evidence: api/tokens.py imports_target=true, imports_source=false, fake_target_added_code=false, target_provider_added=false
reasons: api/tokens.py imports and meaningfully uses aiohttp.ClientSession/session.request
requests import was removed and no source-library import/use is reported in changed production code
target aiohttp origin is the installed site-packages package, with target_local_spec_count 0

+class _AiohttpRequests:

+    def get(self, url, **kwargs):

+    async def _request_async(self, method, url, **kwargs):

+                return _OAuth2Response(response.status, payload)
